From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Emma Thompson <emma.thompson@velopay.com>
Cc: support@velopay.com
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Velopay: bridge playbook and roadmap clarifications for tonight's latency spike

Team / Emma —

Thanks for hopping on the bridge earlier. Velopay saw a ~3x p95 jump between 12:55–13:10 PDT that correlated with a sudden fan-out of short requests (user auth checks + invoice previews). Emma, you already shared the request patterns via support@ — appreciate that.

We need quick alignment on:
- What SRE action will be taken in the next 90 mins (and who owns the postmortem).
- Product asks: do we provide a temporary rate-limit tweak and a tokenized prefix cache for invoice-preview endpoints?
- Customer comms: Marissa, please review the short note below for Velopay.

Attachments: bridge-playbook-v2.docx (latest runbook), latency-metrics-20280327.csv (ingested traces).
Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/654321
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HP-45272

Quick asks:
- Ben: can you confirm if the autoscaler spiked GPUs or throttled on our side?
- Karthik: do we have a safe rollback or quick toggle for the new KV-cache heuristic we shipped last week?
- Soojin: can you prepare a one-paragraph customer-friendly note (I drafted below)?

Proposed customer message (draft):
"Hi Emma — we saw an elevated latency window around 12:55–13:10 PDT caused by a sudden increase in concurrent short requests. Our SREs applied a short-term rate cap and a cache adjustment to stabilize latency; we will follow up with a root-cause and remediation plan within 24 hours. —Olga"

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Emma Thompson <emma.thompson@velopay.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Velopay: bridge playbook and roadmap clarifications for tonight's latency spike

On Tue, Mar 27, 2028 at 13:02, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / Emma —
>
> Thanks for hopping on the bridge earlier. Velopay saw a ~3x p95 jump...

Quick triage update from infra:
- Autoscaler did not add GPUs; autoscaler metrics show a CPU-based throttling on the gen-api nodes (high context-switching due to many very short requests).
- We applied a per-tenant token bucket cap (rate limit) at 13:15 PDT for Velopay to reduce fan-out. Immediate effect: p95 dropped ~40% by 13:25 (see attached csv).
- Root cause hypothesis: the recent client-side batching change (invoice preview) increased concurrent small requests; KV cache TTL interaction caused hot-keying on a small set of shards.

Next steps I own:
1) Rebalance shard mapping for Velopay traffic (eta 2 hours).
2) Add a temporary KV TTL override rule (30m -> 2h) for invoice-preview prefixes; conservative -- low risk.
3) Preserve traces and hand off to product for longer-term change.

I will keep sampling on the bridge and post logs to the shared Drive.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency-metrics-20280327.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Emma Thompson <emma.thompson@velopay.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Velopay: bridge playbook and roadmap clarifications for tonight's latency spike

Thanks for the rapid triage. A few product notes:
- The KV-cache heuristic rolled last Thursday can be toggled via the rollout service. We can flip the heuristic OFF for Velopay prefixes and observe; low-risk but we need to know traffic shape. Ben, are the hot keys pinned to a small prefix list you can share?
- If the customer prefers not to change client batching immediately, product can ship a targeted mitigation: prefix-based pre-warming + tighter cache-miss rate limiting. That would be a small code change (1 week) but we can provide a config toggle in 24 hours.

For customer communication: I recommend we include a short line that a temporary config change was applied (rate cap + cache tweak) and that engineering will follow with a targeted fix and a timeline.

Action items assigned:
- Ben: share hot-key list + expected impact of TTL override (by 15:00).
- Marissa: send the customer note (below) and Cc me for product timeline commitments.

-Karthik
Director, Product — Serving Runtime

Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Velopay stabilization summary and next steps

Emma / Velopay ops —

Thank you — the quick bridge and the log bundle you shared were very helpful. Summary of what happened and what we did:
- Incident window: ~12:55–13:10 PDT. Observed ~3x p95 spike for the gen-api path used by invoice preview.
- Immediate mitigation (13:15): tenant-level rate cap + temporary KV TTL override for invoice-preview prefixes. P95 improved ~40% within 10 minutes.
- Owner & timeline: Ben owns rebalance + short-term shard fix (ETA ~2 hours). Karthik owns product follow-up: targeted pre-warming + config toggle (ETA 24–72 hours depending on rollout). I will produce the incident summary + timeline and share within 24 hours.

Attached: bridge-playbook-v2.docx; latency-metrics-20280327.csv; link to the bridge recording: https://zoom.us/rec/share/zoom-recording-20280327
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HP-45272

We will follow up with a postmortem and a recommended change to the rollout policy to avoid hot-key fan-out in similar patterns. If you want us to file a joint status page entry, Marissa is prepared to post.

Best,
Olga
